attrs.evidence: FAC-ARTIFACT-CANONICAL-MATCH bound every path IN the commit and left every path outside it to a filename pattern. GPT-5.6 reproduced both consequences on a clean extraction of INV-R8.2: an invented `fake-proof-output.txt` containing arbitrary text asserting everything passed was admitted because its suffix matched `*-output.txt`, and the REAL `mosaic-gate-output.txt` was rewritten in place — bundle untouched — and also passed. Both reproduced here before the repair. A FILENAME MATCHING A BUILD-PRODUCT GLOB IS NOT A FILE THAT BUILD PRODUCED, and these are the files that look most like evidence to a human reader: captured gate output, which the archive's own front page invites a reviewer to compare against their own run. Which capture belongs to which kind was MEASURED, not assumed: all ten were re-run inside a clean extraction and diffed. Seven reproduce (one modulo the gate's own elapsed-time line, under a normalisation bounded to that one line); three do not, for three distinct reasons, each stated in its declaration. Enforced in two places that need each other: scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs re-runs the derived commands against a real extraction, and check-mosaic §6 checks the DECLARATION shape, which is registry data and therefore portable to a tree with no git.
attrs.gap: INTERNAL CONSISTENCY, NOT AUTHENTICITY — unchanged, and inherited whole from FAC-ARTIFACT-CANONICAL-MATCH. An attacker who rewrites a capture, rebuilds the bundle and re-runs the gates passes this, because nothing is signed; FAC-RECEIPT-AUTH is that record and is open. Second, THE UNTRUSTED SET IS THE RESIDUE AND IT IS NOT EMPTY: THE UNTRUSTED SET IS NOT EMPTY and this sentence deliberately does not say how large it is — the gate derives that (brief-facts {{ARTIFACT_UNTRUSTED_COUNT}}). INV-R8.3 wrote a literal here and it was wrong, and the honest statement is that they are labelled rather than checked. Third, `factory-scope-output.txt` is the sharpest of them — it is a capture of a run against the SOURCE tree and it ships inside an artifact with two more narrative paths than it reports, so it was never wrong about the tree it measured and it accompanies a different one. Making it derivable means running the classifier after staging rather than before, which changes what the build does and is not attempted here. Fourth: a `derived` declaration could in principle name a command that reads the shipped capture, which would compare a file to itself; nothing mechanical refuses that yet.
attrs.implementation_binding: scripts/verify-review-artifact.mjs — the classified-additions section and --selftest; scripts/check-mosaic.mjs — P.artifactAdditionsTyped and mutations MUT-ARTIFACT-*
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R8.2, §artifact. The derived/untrusted split is the two options that audit named. The re-derivation half is what reproducible-build verification does — rebuild and compare rather than trust a label — narrowed here to build products of a single archive.
attrs.review_focus: Two questions. (1) The re-derivation composes with the canonical check rather than duplicating it — the gate being re-run is itself a committed path already byte-compared, so an attacker cannot make capture and generator agree by editing the generator. Is that composition actually closed, or is there an ordering in which it is not? (2) `untrusted_capture` is an honest label and also a hole: nothing mechanical stops a future product being declared untrusted BECAUSE re-deriving it is inconvenient. The non-consumption rule is the only enforcement, and it constrains what may rest on such a file without constraining how many there may be.
attrs.statement: Every file in a review extraction that is NOT a byte of the canonical commit is admitted by exact name and declares a kind: a `derived` product carries the command that produced it and is re-run and compared here, and an `untrusted_capture` is declared not-evidence, states what the extraction lacks, and may not be reached by any derivation.
